newsitem.title: USA: EMERGING DEBT SLIPS LATE WITH U.S. TREASURIES.
newsitem.headline: EMERGING DEBT SLIPS LATE WITH U.S. TREASURIES.

text.p: Emerging market debt turned narrowly mixed late on Thursday after a technicals-based decline in the U.S. Treasury market, traders said.
Most Brady bond prices had risen modestly in thin volume before the September T-bond futures contract broke through support at 114-16/32, sparking a selloff in both markets.
Yield spreads narrowed as emerging debt prices dipped less severely than those of U.S. Treasuries.
"Most of the selling in our market is coming from the Street right now," one Brady trader said. "Client accounts have been quiet all day."
Russian issues again led the rest of the emerging debt market on Thursday. Vnesh loans shot to record levels in European trading and added to their gains in the U.S. session.
"There have been very good buyers of the Russian dollar loans -- people switching out of cash," one head Brady trader said.
Anticipation of the country's London Club debt restructuring prompted buying, the trader said, even though the closing date for the reconciliation has been pushed to yearend from October.
Dollar-denominated Vnesh jumped two percentage points to 100-7/8 as they rose above par for the first time, traders said.
Among key Latin American issues, benchmark Brazil "C" bonds were off 1/4 at 83-5/8, while Pars were unchanged at 72-1/8.
A Brazil Senate panel voted to approve Gustavo Franco as the new central bank president. The full floor of the Senate will vote on Franco's nomination next Tuesday.
Elsewhere, Argentina FRBs were off 1/8 at 95-1/2, and Mexico Pars fell 3/8 to 81-1/2.
Traders said they expected the market to remain range-bound in the days ahead.
"We're going to continue trading in a range," one said. "I think it's good for the market to take a breath, to see spreads widening a little bit."
